title: Rank the evidence, not just find it
statement: In an evidence hunt, label each phrase a student can pick as key clue, other clue, weaker detail or distractor, give each its own feedback, then ask which is strongest.
detail: A Grade 3 inference design breaks its modelled passage into short tappable phrases and labels each as a clue, an interesting detail or a distractor, with one compulsory key clue. Each label gets its own feedback, and once the clues are collected a quality check asks which clue best describes what the character wants. The Grade 3 standards sheet names the usual failure in choosing evidence as picking a random, interesting or nearby detail instead of the relevant one.
